question: How are big banks limiting group lawsuits in their customer contracts?
answer: Through their customer agreements: across 12 dated records from November 2018 to June 4, 2026, the library documents 8 banks and card issuers (Bank of America, Bread / Comenity, Chase, Citi, Cross River, PNC, Synchrony, Truist) using individual arbitration, waivers of class and group claims, and short mailed opt-out windows, and 3 records add special rules for mass filings. Each card links the contract or notice it comes from.

sections.title: Bank by bank
sections.sub: Each card is one contract, notice or letter, with the bank's legal entity named.

items.key: fine:2018-11:comenity s notice and cure mac
items.title: Comenity's notice-and-cure machinery already in place
kv: The November 2018 forms already required at least thirty days' pre-suit notice and a cure period, an individually retained lawyer, and a personally signed arbitration rejection. They also offered a $5,100 special payment to a claimant who beat the bank's rejected pre-demand offer — an incentive the current form no longer contains. The baseline matters: the hardening did not begin in 2025. It deepened.

items.key: fine:2023-06-14:cross river s own terms take e
items.title: Cross River's own terms take effect
items.sub: 2023-06-14 · Cross River Bank; CRB Group, Inc.
kv: Individual AAA arbitration, class and representative waiver, a sixty-day pre-arbitration notice period, and a thirty-day mailed opt-out after account opening. Covered parties reach the bank and its broadly defined affiliates, officers, agents and representatives. Notably, a customer may reject a future arbitration change within thirty days and keep the earlier language — a right most of the big banks do not grant.
Cross River Bank; CRB Group, Inc.

items.title: Chase replaces its deposit-account arbitration section
kv: The change notice replaced the arbitration section outright and gave existing customers until January 16, 2025 to opt out by phone. The replacement reaches past, present and future claims — accounts, transactions, products, services, advertising, applications, denials, approvals, employees, agents. It bars class, representative, consolidated and public-injunctive relief. And the definition of "we" expands: if Chase assigns the account to an unaffiliated third party, that assignee is folded into the protected class. The shield is written to travel with the debt.

items.title: Chase's mass-arbitration machine
kv: The current Deposit Account Agreement defines a mass arbitration at twenty-five or more coordinated claims and builds a procedure for it: claimant-specific transaction facts, damages calculations and authorization; a process arbitrator empowered to screen and dismiss at the threshold; sanctions; and an initial thirty cases — fifteen chosen by each side — sent through merits arbitration before any later rounds. Customers may opt out only within sixty days of opening the account. The provision continues after closure, after full payment, and after bankruptcy.

sources.label: Chase Deposit Account Agreement, current edition

items.title: Citi's deposit agreement closes the door behind you
kv: Individual AAA arbitration, no class or representative or combined claims, and a forty-five-day mailed opt-out — but only for new accounts. Customers who failed to reject under the prior agreement do not get a new opt-out. The relationship is defined as debtor-creditor, not fiduciary. Citi keeps setoff without notice against most accounts for debts of an owner or beneficial owner, and may close with or without cause. Arbitration survives termination, bankruptcy, and sale of the account or the debt.

items.title: Truist's deposit agreement demands a handwritten signature
kv: Individual JAMS arbitration, a required pre-dispute notice and informal-resolution period, express recognition of mass-arbitration procedures, and a thirty-day opt-out that must be personally signed and sent certified or overnight. Arbitration demands themselves require personally handwritten signatures. Class, consolidated, collective and representative relief are all barred. Truist may close without cause or notice and exercise setoff for debts owed to Truist and related entities.

items.title: Truist rewrites arbitration inside the app agreement
kv: Truist's official notice adds instant-network bill pay and instant external transfers, moves limits and cutoffs into the app itself, revises the service-guarantee conditions — and changes the mutual arbitration, jury-waiver and litigation-class-waiver provisions. The dispute terms now ride in the same document as the transfer limits.

items.title: Synchrony batches the crowd into groups of fifty
kv: The current CareCredit agreement (revision code 3/2026) carries a "MASS FILING PROCEDURES" section: coordinated demands "shall be grouped into batches of no more than 50 demands per batch by state of residence, and then alphabetically by last name… One Merits Arbitrator shall be assigned for each batch, who shall provide for resolution of each batch as a single arbitration with one set of filing and administrative fees." Plus a mandatory individualized Notice of Dispute, a sixty-day informal-resolution period, and Rule 11-style certification. The same architecture appears in the PayPal card terms — it is not merchant-specific.
The source packet dated this 2026-01-01; that date is not established. The revision code is the defensible anchor.

items.title: The Bank of America agreement that has no arbitration clause
kv: The Online Banking Service Agreement in force on this date — still the live document at the bank's own URL as of the audit — contains no arbitration section at all. The word does not appear. This is the "before" state, and it is the honest one: it tightens the insertion window to under eight weeks and it does not depend on the Internet Archive.

sources.label: Bank of America — Online Banking Service Agreement

items.key: fine:2026-05-18:bank of america builds a dispu
items.title: Bank of America builds a dispute constitution for the whole digital layer
kv: The replacement agreement inserts a full §12, "Disputes and Arbitration," into a bank agreement that had none. Its scope is not a checking account. It reaches, in the document's own words, "Zelle Network Services, Real Time Payment Network Service, Bill Payment Services, ACH, Wire and Internal Transfer Services, E-Bills, Online Banking Alerts, BankAmeriDeals, and Erica Bank of America's Virtual Financial Assistant" — and "the application for, or the denial, approval or establishment of your Online/Mobile ID account."

sources.label: Bank of America — May 18 2026 agreement update

items.key: fine:2026-06-04:three senators write to bank o
items.title: Three senators write to Bank of America
kv: Senators Blumenthal, Warren and Johnson write to the bank about the newly adopted forced-arbitration provision. The National Consumer Law Center and a Public Citizen coalition letter make the same objection. The independent record confirms what the documents show: this was new, and it was noticed.

sources.label: Senate letter to Bank of America

items.title: PNC's arbitration reaches the assets of failed banks
kv: Individual arbitration; waivers of class, private-attorney-general, representative and joined claims. The definition of who is protected reaches affiliates, predecessors, acquired entities, successors, assigns — and assets acquired from failed banks. Customers get a forty-five-day mailed opt-out, but later amendments do not reopen it unless PNC changes a substantive arbitration clause.

The library's own framing of these records: The consumer side of the money story, 2018→2028 — the paper an ordinary person signs. Five tracks: the crowd taken apart, the brand held still while the bank behind it changes, the credit placed where the wanting is, the customer's own data sold back as a product, and the question of who actually owns the debt. A reading of the record, not a claim of one signed plan — every bank here has a …
Contracts change without notice; a card shows the agreement as of its date, not necessarily today's terms.

catalog_context.title: What big banks are building, and the fine print behind it
catalog_context.answer: Big banks are growing by tying checking, cards, installment loans, payments and customer data into one relationship, and using AI to approve and personalize.
catalog_context.read_first: vault:02 - Research/Banking Website Sweep — Source Document.md

catalog_context.title: Banks are moving card debt to firms willing to hold it, not forgiving it
catalog_context.answer: Big lenders are selling or buying whole debt books and moving more struggling cardholders into low-rate fixed payment plans. Very little of this is forgiveness: a sale, a charge-off or a new servicer does not wipe out what the borrower owes.
